Date: 2026-06-24

Attendees: Ava Ramirez (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (CTO, Stellar), Elena Gomez (Platform), Markus Chen (SRE)
summary: POC scoping focused on defining latency and throughput SLOs for a pilot integration. Discussed TTFT vs TPOT, p95/p99 targets, workload sizing (QPS, batch sizes), hardware constraints, and a measurement/benchmarking plan. Agreed next steps: Redwood shares benchmark plan and test prompts; customer supplies traffic profile; schedule SE-led benchmark run.
topics: TTFT vs TPOT definitions and relevance
Workload sizing: QPS, burst, tokens per request
Timeline for POC and success criteria
transcript:
[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll run 45 minutes or so, quick intros?
[00:07] Ravi: Hey, Ravi here, CTO, dealing with inference infra and cost targets.
[00:12] Elena: Elena, platform eng, owns latency SLOs and ingress.
[00:16] Marcus: Marcus from Redwood, SE, I'll drive the benchmark details.
[00:21] Markus: Markus, SRE, curious about p99 behavior and degrade modes.
[00:26] Ava: Great. The goal today is to get concrete SLOs and a measurement plan for the POC, agree success criteria. Marcus, want to start with TTFT vs TPOT?
[00:34] Marcus: Sure. TTFT is time-to-first-token — important for perceived latency, e.g., chat experiences. TPOT is time-per-output-token or sometimes time-to-last-token depending on definition — more about throughput and sustained costs. For your interactive UI we usually target TTFT tightness for snappy replies and then TPOT matters for long completions or streaming.
[01:02] Ravi: For us, two main surfaces: agent chat (snappy) and batch summarization (high throughput). So we need both TTFT and TPOT SLOs.
[01:10] Elena: Question, how do you measure TTFT in the wild? Is it measured at gateway or at the GPU? We have load balancers and an API gateway, upstream network adds variance.
[01:20] Marcus: Good point. We recommend measuring at two points: "edge TTFT" (what the client sees, includes network/gateway) and "service TTFT" (time when the model first token is produced at the runtime). For POC we can capture both — Redwood agent collects service-level timings, you can capture client-side timing in your app.
[01:40] Markus: And p95/p99 — we care about p99 tail. For example our current hard SLO is p99 < 800ms for small replies; anything above triggers paging.
[01:49] Marcus: For interactive chat we usually advise: TTFT p95 = 200-300ms, p99 = 500-700ms on dedicated GPU pools; on hosted tiers, p99 may be higher (1s+), depends on batching and cold starts. For TPOT, for steady-state token generation we look at throughput tokens/sec or ms/token — p95 throughput stable within X% of median.
[02:15] Elena: Those numbers sound optimistic. Our current self-hosted endpoints have TTFT p99 around 1.2s for 256-token completions. We need to know what hardware and config to expect for the POC.
[02:27] Marcus: For the POC we'll test on a dedicated small pool (A100-ish equivalent) with quantized model variants. We'll enumerate config: batch sizes, KV cache enabled, prompt prefixes, and sequence lengths. We'll run a baseline with single-request TTFT and a load test to measure TPOT at target QPS.
[02:45] Ava: Let's capture workload sizing — what QPS do you expect for chat?
[02:50] Ravi: Peak for chat 60 QPS, average 20 QPS, median request size ~120 tokens in, 80 tokens out. For batch summarization: spike jobs at 200 concurrent requests but they are queued and can be asynchronous.
[03:05] Marcus: Good. For 60 QPS interactive with 80-token outputs we need to understand batching impact. If we batch aggressively we might improve throughput but increase TTFT. So measurement plan will include varying batching window (0, 5ms, 20ms) and measuring TTFT p95/p99 and tokens/sec.
[03:25] Markus: Also need to test canary fallbacks — if dedicated pool saturates, how does Redwood route to hosted variants? We want graceful degradation with explicit SLA changes.
[03:33] Ava: We'll include routing/fallback scenarios. Next, success criteria for POC — what does Stellar need to consider it a win?
[03:39] Ravi: Three things: 1) TTFT p95 <= 350ms for our chat flow; p99 <= 700ms, 2) TPOT sustained enough to handle 60 QPS with median output latency within 20% of target, 3) cost per 1M tokens less than $X (we'll provide target).
[03:56] Elena: Add runbook and instrumentation: must produce traces and token-level cost breakdown.
[04:02] Marcus: We'll surface token-level cost and latency breakdowns in the Redwood Console and include per-route dashboards. For the benchmark, we'll produce an artifacts bundle: raw timings, percentile calculations, histograms, and sample logs. We'll also provide a measurement script you can run inside your VPC if doing private deployment.
[04:22] Ravi: Measurement definitions — we need to standardize how p95 and p99 are computed: across requests including retries? across tokens?
[04:31] Marcus: Good call. Measurement plan: compute TTFT per request measured at service runtime (timestamp request received at runtime -> first token emitted). Exclude retries from baseline (but run a separate retry/cold-start test). For TPOT measure ms/token after first token until last token averaged per request, and report tokens/sec and ms/token percentiles. We'll also capture end-to-end client-side metrics to ensure network contribution is known.
[04:57] Elena: For p95/p99 we prefer windowed calculation over 5-minute windows to capture transient spikes.
[05:03] Marcus: We'll provide both rolling 5-minute percentiles and the overall test percentiles. Benchmarks will include: single-request latency, steady-state sustained QPS ramp up, burst/chaos (spikes), and cold-start scenarios.
[05:18] Markus: What about sampling frequency and telemetry retention? We need granularity for debugging tails.
[05:24] Marcus: We'll push request-level traces with 1s resolution and event timestamps; Redwood Console retains full traces for the POC period; we can also supply raw CSV export.
[05:34] Ravi: Timeline? We need POC results within 2 weeks.
[05:38] Ava: Proposed timeline: 1) By 6/26 Redwood shares benchmark plan and prompts, 2) Customer provides traffic profile by 6/29, 3) SE-led benchmark run 6/30 (90 min), 4) Analysis and report by 7/02, decision meeting 7/03. Does that work?
[05:54] Elena: Yes.
[05:55] Marcus: I'll outline the test matrix: matrix dimensions: model variant (full/quantized), batch sizes (1, 4, 8), batching window (0/5/20ms), sequence lengths (short/medium/long), QPS points (10, 20, 60, 100 burst). We'll measure TTFT p50/p95/p99, TPOT ms/token p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, CPU/GPU utilization, and cost per 1k tokens.
[06:30] Markus: For dedicated vs hosted we need estimated deltas — please include historical numbers if possible.
[06:35] Marcus: We'll include prior benchmark references; note hosted often has 1.2–1.5x higher p99 due to multi-tenant queueing. Dedicated pools typically hit our lower TTFT bands. We'll call out cold-start windows for private deployments too.
[06:50] Ravi: Security and compliance — we'll need SOC2 docs and KMS encryption for private. Also audit logs for token access.
[06:58] Ava: We'll attach Redwood security pack and a link to our SOC2 summary. We'll also include KMS integration notes for private deployment.
[07:07] Elena: One more operational ask: define success thresholds per route — chat vs batch summarization — and a rollback criteria if p99 exceeds threshold during POC.
[07:16] Marcus: Add to plan: per-route SLOs and automated rollback criteria (e.g., sustained p99 > threshold for 3 consecutive 5-min windows triggers canary rollback).
[07:26] Ava: Ok let's recap next steps and owners. Marcus will run the test harness and define scripts; Ava will share benchmark plan and pricing; Elena will collect traffic profile; Markus will join SE-run.
[07:40] Ravi: Sounds good. Thanks all.
[07:43] Ava: Thanks, we'll send notes and checklist.
[07:47] (call ends)

Notes: transcription shows timestamps roughly every 30-90s; occasional words may be slightly off ("Kubernates" instead of Kubernetes). References: benchmark plan doc (link: https://redwood-internal/benchmarks/stellar-poc), security pack (link: https://redwood-internal/security/soc2.pdf).
notes: Key measurement definitions: TTFT = request_received_at_runtime -> first_token_emitted; TPOT = per-token generation time after first token. Percentiles: report p50/p95/p99 and rolling 5-min windows. Test matrix includes model variant, batch sizes, batching window, sequence lengths, and QPS points. Success criteria: TTFT p95 <= 350ms, p99 <= 700ms for chat route; TPOT within 20% of median throughput at 60 QPS; cost target to be provided by customer.
recap: Agreed POC timeline and deliverables: benchmark plan by 2026-06-26, traffic profile by 2026-06-29, SE-led run on 2026-06-30, analysis by 2026-07-02, decision meeting 2026-07-03.
